formatting.fileFormat: Word document ('For submission and review, please submit the manuscript as a Word document. Do not submit your manuscript in PDF format.'). Manuscript file holds title page, abstract, text, references, and as appropriate figure legends and tables; figures are submitted as separate files (1 file per figure); tables go at the end of the manuscript file, not as images or separate files.
formatting.margins: right margins unjustified (ragged); no margin width is stated
formatting.pageNumbers: 'Start each of these sections on a new page, numbered consecutively, beginning with the title page.'
formatting.referenceStyle: AMA Manual of Style, 11th edition. Number references in the order they appear in the text (do not alphabetize); superscript Arabic numerals in text, tables, and legends; list all authors up to 6, if more than 6 list the first 3 followed by 'et al'; journal names abbreviated per PubMed; issue number in parentheses after the volume number. AI, LLM, and chatbots must not be used to generate or format references.
formatting.coverLetter: Required. 'Include a cover letter and complete contact information for the corresponding author (affiliation, postal/mail address, email address, and telephone number) and whether the authors have published, posted, or submitted any related papers from the same study.'
formatting.supplement: Online-only supplement submitted as a single Word document with consecutively numbered pages; first page lists every element by number and title; cite each element in the text and number in order of citation (eTable 1, eFigure 1, eMethods). Text Arial 10 point single-spaced; main headings 12 point bold; subheadings 10 point bold; table and figure titles Arial 12 point bold; footnotes and legends 8 point. Supplement must not repeat print material and must be limited and justified. The Data Sharing Statement is published in the supplement; the PRISMA-style flow diagram for systematic reviews goes in the supplement; Research Letters may use a supplement only for brief additional Methods. Large datasets belong in public repositories.
formatting.titlePage: First page of the manuscript file. Must include: the manuscript title; full names, highest academic degrees, and affiliations of all authors (if an affiliation changed since the work was done, list the new affiliation too); name and complete contact information for the corresponding author; manuscript word count (not including title, abstract, acknowledgment, references, tables, and figure legends). Key Points are a separate section placed before the Abstract.

abstracts.other: Meta-analysis: structured abstract of no more than 350 words with headings Importance, Objective, Data Sources, Study Selection, Data Extraction and Synthesis, Main Outcome(s) and Measure(s), Results, Conclusions and Relevance. Clinical trials: 'trial registration information (registry name, trial ID, and URL) must be listed at the end of the abstract'. Design, Setting, and Participants are kept as separate headings at submission. Results must open with summary demographic information and the number of participants. 'Abstracts are not required for Editorials, Viewpoints, and special features.' Research Letters have no abstract. Do not use abbreviations in the title or abstract.

keyPoints.rules: 'In the manuscript, include a separate section called "Key Points" before the Abstract.' Required only for research and review manuscripts (not Research Letters, Narrative Reviews, Viewpoints, Letters). 'Limit this section to 75-100 words or less.' Question: 'Focused question based on the study hypothesis or goal/purpose. Limit to 1 sentence.' Findings: results of the study/review including the design; focus on primary outcome(s); report basic numbers only and state whether results are statistically significant; do not include results of statistical tests or measures of variance; 'Can include 1 to 2 sentences.' Meaning: 'Key conclusion and implication based on the primary finding(s). Limit to 1 sentence.'

journalNotes: The instructions page is a JAMA Network shared document; article-type applicability was taken from the page's Include/Exclude journal directives (codes JAMA, CAR, DER, IMD, NEU, ONC, OPH, PED, OTO, PSY, SUR, JNO, JHF) and the journal's Categories of Articles table (which lists Original Investigation, Research Letter, Systematic Review, Narrative Review, Viewpoint, Letter to the Editor, Letter in Reply).

Editor: Melina R. Kibbe, MD, University of Virginia. Submission site: https://manuscripts.jamasurg.com/. For-authors page: JAMA Surgery 'is the official publication of the Association of VA Surgeons, the Pacific Coast Surgical Association' (and other societies) and offers the 'Opportunity to publish new research simultaneously with your presentation'; no separate submission rules for association/society papers are given.

Surgical Innovation and Pacific Coast Surgical Association papers do NOT appear on the instructions page; no limits could be recorded for them. 'Guide to Statistics and Methods' (linked from the for-authors page at /journals/jamasurgery/pages/statistics-and-methods) is a reader-facing collection of published articles with no author instructions.

Clinical Challenge: the page's directives are self-contradictory for SUR ('Include: NEU, ONC, OTO, SUR' while the same block's Exclude list also contains SUR; another block excludes SUR) and the page contains no Clinical Challenge description or limits, so it is not recorded as an article type.

Special Communication is excluded for SUR by both of its directives ('Exclude: IMD, JNO, SUR' and 'Exclude: SUR') and is absent from the journal's Categories table. Brief Report is not listed in the Categories table and the specific Brief Report directives exclude SUR (a broader 'JAMA and SJs' directive conflicts). Humanities features, Consensus Statement, Clinical Practice Guidelines, and Caring for the Critically Ill Patient are excluded for SUR.

Both review types (Systematic Review and Narrative Review) require a presubmission inquiry for this journal (directive 'Include: JAMA, PED, SUR'), with an outline, literature summary (or draft), and publication record sent by email to Gerard Doherty, MD (address obfuscated on the page).
Editorials and Invited Commentaries are not listed as submission categories (the page only says 'Abstracts are not required for Editorials, Viewpoints, and special features').
Key Points are required for research and review manuscripts and are not used for Research Letters, Narrative Reviews, Viewpoints, or Letters.

Data Sharing Statement required for all reports of research; published in an online supplement. Authorship: ICMJE 4 criteria; group byline for more than 50 authors; the Access to Data statement must use the exact wording by at least 1 and no more than 2 named authors.
File sizes: individual files no more than 500 kB recommended and not exceeding 1 MB; total for all files not exceeding 5 MB (excluding video). Each figure generally no larger than 1 MB at submission.

Figures: separate file per figure; no more than 4 panels unless justified; photographs/illustrations >=350 ppi, line drawings >=600 ppi; vector formats preferred; no pie charts, 3-D graphs, or stacked bar charts; titles preferably 10-15 words; figures with markers need versions with and without markers.
Tables: at the end of the manuscript file; single-spaced 10- or 12-point; titles preferably 10-15 words; minimum 2 columns; frequencies as 'No. (%)'; footnotes with superscript letters.

Video: .mov/.wmv/.mpg/.mpeg/.mp4/.avi, max 25 MB at submission, preferred length <=5 minutes, title max 100 characters, caption 1-5 sentences, description 3-10 sentences; identifiable patients need a signed permission form and faces may not be blurred. Audio: .mp3/.wav/.aiff, max 25 MB, max 5 minutes, 44.1 or 48 kHz.

Patient identification: 'A signed statement of informed consent to publish patient descriptions, photographs, video, and pedigrees should be obtained'; do not submit masked photographs; no identifiers in images.

Timeliness: RCTs ideally within 1 year after follow-up completed; cohort studies' final follow-up no more than 5 years before submission; case-control and cross-sectional data no more than 5 years old; older data receive lower priority.

Statistics: Statistical Analysis subsection at the end of Methods; P values never alone (P<.001; nearest thousandth between .001 and .01; nearest hundredth at or above .01; P>.99); baseline characteristics tables should not include P values; causal language only for RCTs; EQUATOR reporting guidelines required.

AI: AI use must be reported in the Acknowledgment; AI must not generate or format references; AI drafting not permitted for Viewpoints and Letters to the Editor. 'Authors should not release information about accepted manuscripts via social media until publication.'
Open access option: $6000 fee (CC-BY-NC-ND or CC-BY). Page footer: 'Last Updated: September 8, 2026'.
unread: All 229,617 characters of the page were fetched in three chunks (0, 100000, 200000) via WebFetch; the final chunk (demographics, ethics, AI policy, journal policies) contains no submission limits. The fetcher caps quotes at 125 characters, so longer sentences in 'quotes' were reconstructed from consecutive fragments. The page text is the JAMA Network master document with journal directives, so journal applicability was resolved from those directives and the journal-specific Categories table; the presubmission-inquiry email address is obfuscated. Surgical Innovation, Pacific Coast Surgical Association papers, and Clinical Challenge limits are not on the page and were not recorded.
